chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah, the Exalted, support him — informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, all together from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about tayammum, so he struck the ground with his right hand, then raised it and shook it off, then wiped with it his forehead and his two palms once.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: dry ablution performed in place of wudu (ablution) or ghusl (ritual bath) under specific conditions
key_terms.الْأَرْضَ: the earth or ground, the surface struck for tayammum
key_terms.بِيَدِهِ الْيُمْنَى: with his right hand, indicating the hand used in the demonstrated act
key_terms.جَبِينَهُ: his forehead, the part of the face wiped in this act
key_terms.فَنَفَضَهَا: then he shook it off, meaning he removed excess dust from the hand
key_terms.كَفَّيْهِ: his two palms, which were wiped as part of the tayammum
key_terms.مَرَّةً وَاحِدَةً: one time, indicating that the wiping was done once

ai.seo_question: How is tayammum performed according to the hadith of Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of tayammum as demonstrated by Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It indicates a practical legal form of dry ablution involving striking the earth, removing excess dust, and wiping the forehead and palms once.
